note: Generated from the programme's use case archive — do not edit by hand. Every case here was published by the person who did the work, through the app's consent step, having chosen a public destination. Rows consented to as private-archive, and rows since withdrawn, are excluded by construction.

cases.author: WW
cases.what: Put the reference material behind a menu so the landing page is the two things people open it to do.
cases.why: A setup guide, a run sheet, ground rules and four reassurances sat above and below create-a-programme and open-a-programme. On a phone that is a lot of scrolling past what a facilitator reads once.
cases.how: A drawer with three tabs — Sheets, Guide, Notices. Which notices stay on the page became a rule with a name rather than an accident of layout: would somebody be entitled to be annoyed at finding this out later? Storage that vanishes with the browser qualifies, and so does recording other people's names and work.
cases.outcome: This now works: the page is create, list, and two notices, with five more a tap away. Tests pin the split, because the failure mode is a notice quietly demoted into the drawer where nobody looks.
cases.nextStep: Carry the same menu into a running programme, where the tab bar has the same problem.

cases.author: WW
cases.what: Put the way back to a lost programme where the loss is noticed, and let a programme be deleted.
cases.why: Restore from a backup lived inside a programme — exactly where you cannot reach it when the thing you have lost is the programme.
cases.how: Moved it to the start page beside the empty space, with two more honest answers next to it: reconnect the Google Sheet, or reopen the setup link. Also stopped the empty list lying — a storage read that threw was swallowed and looked identical to having no programmes at all.
cases.outcome: This now works: a blocked store says so, and an unreadable one hands back the raw text to save before the next write overwrites it. Deleting is on the card, and the confirmation differs by what is at stake — a sheet-backed programme survives in the sheet, a browser-only one offers a backup before it offers the button.
cases.nextStep: A one-tap template so a programme can be rebuilt when no backup exists.

cases.author: WW
cases.what: Let the public site publish the cases whose authors chose a public destination, and only those.
cases.why: The page read a list maintained by hand. A filter you have to remember to apply is a filter that will one day not be applied.
cases.how: The feed is generated from the archive, and the generation is where the filter lives — public destination and active status only, dropped by construction. Anonymity is enforced twice: the builder drops the author key outright rather than trusting the row's empty string, so a hand-edited archive cannot leak a name through the one file that goes on the internet.
cases.outcome: This now works, and this page is the proof: the cases you are reading came out of that pipeline. Publishing stays a deliberate act — a command that lists what it is about to publish by name, then a diff to read.
cases.nextStep: Show the frame on the page itself, so a reader can sort and filter rather than scroll.

cases.author: WW
cases.what: Turn published use cases into a dataframe, and give it somewhere durable that is mine — a private GitHub repository.
cases.why: A use case is prose. Counting them, charting them, or handing them to somebody else's spreadsheet needs one row per case with fixed columns, and the consent that permits the row travelling in the row.
cases.how: A 21-column frame with JSONL as the record and CSV and TSV regenerated from it. Where a case goes became part of what its author agrees to, so a push to a repository that turns out to be public is refused outright when any row on it says private-archive. Anonymity is structural: no name, no participant id, no key derived from one.
cases.outcome: This now works: the table copies straight into a Google Sheet or downloads as CSV for pandas, and pushes to a private repository as five files — the record, two views, a column reference and a NOTICE generated from the rows themselves, so it cannot claim an archive is private while a public row sits below it.
cases.nextStep: Add an optional scope reference column for VAF basket, SIA stage or CORENET X gateway.
cases.tools: Claude Code; TypeScript; GitHub API; Node

cases.author: WW
cases.what: Let the sprint log reach a spreadsheet with no script and no deployment, in about a minute.
cases.why: Connecting a sheet is worth ten minutes when several people write to one board. For one person keeping a record it is ten minutes of nothing.
cases.how: Tab-separated rows behind a Copy button, pasted at cell A1. A spreadsheet paste splits on tabs and newlines and ignores CSV quoting, so line breaks inside an answer are flattened to a middot — and the page says so rather than leaving it to be discovered.
cases.outcome: This now works from a phone, where downloading a CSV and importing it does not. The page states the trade-off in a table: a snapshot in a minute, or a sheet that stays current for ten.
cases.nextStep: Answer the question people actually arrive with, which is why the sheet is still empty.

cases.author: WW
cases.what: Make the whole Google Sheets setup completable from a phone, and give it a checkpoint that runs before deploying.
cases.why: The setup asked someone to fetch a script from a repository, which is exactly the step that fails when the person holding the phone is the facilitator standing in a meeting room.
cases.how: The app now carries the Apps Script source with a Copy button, so setup never needs the repository. Added a checkSetup function to run from the editor first — it creates the tabs and forces the permission prompt, which splits two failures that otherwise look identical.
cases.outcome: This now works: if checkSetup succeeds, the script is bound to the right sheet and allowed to write to it, so anything still failing is the deployment. If it errors, no deployment will help. The whole setup runs from a phone.
cases.nextStep: Say plainly what a sheet showing one blank Sheet1 actually means.
cases.tools: Claude Code; Google Apps Script; Node

cases.author: WW
cases.what: Give a programme a backup it can actually be restored from, and refuse the files it cannot vouch for.
cases.why: Programmes live in one browser. Clearing site data is an inconvenience only if there is a file to come back from.
cases.how: One file carrying sprints, people, projects, every row, targets and the dropdown lists — deliberately dropping the sheet connection, because a backup gets emailed and copied around and should not also hand over the ability to overwrite the data it restores.
cases.outcome: This now works: a restore states what the file holds and asks first. Wrong file type, wrong version, no programme id or a missing section is each named rather than half-applied, and a participant share bundle offered here is refused and pointed at the tab where it does belong.
cases.nextStep: Put restore somewhere reachable when there is no programme to open.

cases.author: WW
cases.what: Let a participant publish a use case on purpose, with attribution as a real choice rather than a checkbox.
cases.why: The sprint log is a working record full of names, clients and evidence links. The part worth showing strangers is a different, smaller thing, and it needs its own consent.
cases.how: Built it by subtraction: a draft starts from a log row and drops every field that identifies a person, a client or an internal system, then names what it dropped rather than asserting it. Attribution became two separate consent sentences, because asking someone publishing anonymously to agree they are 'credited to the author name shown' records an agreement they never gave.
cases.outcome: This now works: seven identifying fields never travel, the consent statement matches the choice actually made, and a blunt scan flags emails, links and long numbers left in the prose for the author to remove.
cases.nextStep: Make the destination part of the same choice, so a private archive and a public page are different promises.

cases.author: WW
cases.what: Fill the sprint log from the AI chat that did the work, so a participant stops copying seventeen answers across by hand.
cases.why: The answers already exist in the conversation someone just finished. Retyping them at minute 55 is the reason logs go unfilled.
cases.how: Built a prompt that carries the sprint's own number, date and target plus the programme's status, stage and AI-use lists, so the reply comes back in words the log can store. Asked for JSON rather than prose, because a shape the parser can reject beats one it has to guess at. Every proposed change is shown before anything moves.
cases.outcome: This now works: copy one prompt out, paste the reply back, and the row fills. A status outside the list is refused, an off-list AI use is dropped, fractional minutes are skipped — each says so rather than going quietly. Anything that would replace what the participant wrote arrives unticked.
cases.nextStep: Let the same panel read a git log, for sprints where the evidence is commits rather than a chat.
